headline: CRUDE PULLS BACK 2.1% AS YANBU REOPENS
lead: WTI settled $92.12, down 2.1%, the first real give-back after two days running toward $96 on Iran-Hormuz fear. Saudi Arabia just restarted loadings at Yanbu on the Red Sea after the East-West pipeline came back partial, and that's a supply story beating a fear story today.
teaser: Crude gave back 2.1% the day Saudi Arabia restarted Yanbu loadings, cheapening harvest diesel bought today.

one_number.unit: million tons, China September LNG imports
one_number.context: China's LNG imports are headed for a second straight monthly drop on high prices tied to the Mideast war, a demand-side crack in the energy fear trade.

yesterdays_call.note: Crude closed $92.12, down 2.1% and well under the $98.50 call; Yanbu supply news beat the Hormuz fear trade.
yesterdays_call.call_line: Called crude up toward $98.50 ($96.13 when the call was made). It closed at $92.12.

action: Diesel buyers: WTI at **$92.12** is the cheapest print in three sessions; lock the next fuel load now before any bounce back to $94.

sections.title: Crude Gives Back The Fear Premium
sections.body:
- WTI fell 2.1% to **$92.12**, unwinding a chunk of the run toward $96 that Iran-Hormuz headlines built the last two sessions.
- Saudi Arabia just restarted crude loadings at Yanbu on the Red Sea after the East-West pipeline resumed partial service, a real supply fact beating a fear headline.
sections.so_what: Supply news is finally out-trading the Iran headlines; the fear premium is leaking.

sections.title: Grains Drift On Empty China Wires
sections.body:
- Corn eased 0.3% to **$5.22**, beans slipped a penny and a half to $12.87, wheat dropped 0.8% to $6.83; nothing new from China to trade.
- Feedstuffs called it straight: lack of trade headlines sent grain prices eroding lower Monday, and Tuesday didn't fix that.
sections.so_what: No China purchase news means the board drifts on its own weight, not demand.

outside_the_pit.title: Kansas Meatpacking Feels Immigration Raid Disruption
outside_the_pit.body: Industry groups say raids in Texas, Kansas, and Oklahoma are pulling workers off shifts, a labor-supply hit that shows up in packer throughput before it shows up in the box.

watch_list.desc: Weekly export sales; beans under 300K MT keeps the drift alive with no China news to fight it.
WTI below $91.00 confirms the Yanbu unwind is real; a bounce back above $94 says the Hormuz trade isn't done.
USMCA Tri-National talks in Calgary; any friction on ag trade language could jolt grain basis.
